rationale: Both are professional, well-structured catalogues that cover Data, Data Management, Automation, AI and cross-cutting services, and both adopt an 'M365-first, not M365-only' stance. A's distinctive strengths are an explicit three-depth model (audit, roadmap, advisory) and lightning-bolt markers flagging cutting-edge offerings, including data mesh, intelligent process automation and a generative-AI solution service covering RAG versus fine-tuning. However, it omits Microsoft Fabric, a central Microsoft data offering today, and gives no per-service scoping. B is more commercially usable. Every service has a service code, a duration and a fee model. It covers Fabric and Copilot grounding, and adds a Data-for-AI readiness assessment, a weighted platform-selection service with 3-year TCO, eDiscovery readiness, AI proof-of-concept advisory and implementation support. It also names non-Microsoft alternatives concretely (Databricks, Snowflake, n8n, MuleSoft) in line with the 'not its only focus' requirement. B uses one outdated product name (Power Virtual Agents) and signals 'cutting edge' less explicitly. Overall it is the more complete and more actionable catalogue.
